description.en: Stories of the Prophets drawn from the Quran, reliable tafsir, and Ibn Kathir’s Qisas al-Anbiya.
description.ar: قصص الأنبياء مستمدة من القرآن والتفاسير الموثوقة وقصص الأنبياء لابن كثير.

description.en: The life and noble character of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
description.ar: حياة النبي محمد ﷺ وشمائله الكريمة.

description.en: Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, including twelve key figures.
description.ar: صحابة النبي ﷺ، ومنهم اثنا عشر علماً من أعلامهم.

description.en: Short authentic accounts of the Tabi'un, successors, and other righteous predecessors.
description.ar: قبسات قصيرة موثقة من أخبار التابعين ومن بعدهم من السلف.

bio.en: The first human and prophet, taught the names and placed on earth as Allah’s vicegerent.
bio.ar: أول البشر والأنبياء، علّمه الله الأسماء وجعله خليفة في الأرض.

bio.en: A truthful prophet raised to a high station; called people back to Adam’s religion and taught justice and charity.
bio.ar: نبي صدّيق رفعه الله مكاناً عليّاً، دعا الناس إلى دين آبائه وعلّمهم العدل والصدقة.

bio.en: Called his people to worship Allah alone for centuries; those who believed were saved in the Ark from the Flood.
bio.ar: دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله وحده قروناً، ونجّى الله المؤمنين معه في السفينة من الطوفان.

bio.en: Sent to the powerful people of ‘Ad, who were arrogant builders; he called them to worship Allah alone.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى قوم عاد الأقوياء المتجبرين، فدعاهم إلى إفراد الله بالعبادة.

bio.en: Sent to Thamud after ‘Ad; called them to tawhid and warned them concerning the she-camel of Allah.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى ثمود بعد عاد، فدعاهم إلى التوحيد وحذّرهم في شأن ناقة الله.

bio.en: The Friend of Allah and father of the prophets, who broke the idols and called his people to pure tawhid.
bio.ar: خليل الله وأبو الأنبياء، كسّر الأصنام ودعا قومه إلى التوحيد الخالص.

bio.en: Son of Ibrahim, left with his mother Hajar in the barren valley of Makkah; linked to Zamzam and the Ka‘bah.
bio.ar: ابن إبراهيم، تُرك مع أمه هاجر في وادٍ غير ذي زرع بمكة، وارتبط باسم زمزم والبيت.

bio.en: Son of Ibrahim, granted after glad tidings; father of Yaqub and a prophet in the line of guidance.
bio.ar: ابن إبراهيم بُشّر به بعد الكبر، أبو يعقوب ونبي في سلسلة الهداية.

bio.en: Also called Israel; favored with prophethood, father of the twelve tribes including Yusuf.
bio.ar: يُدعى إسرائيل، آتاه الله النبوة، وأبو الأسباط الاثني عشر ومنهم يوسف.

bio.en: Nephew of Ibrahim, sent to the people of Sodom to forbid their open immorality and call them to Allah.
bio.ar: ابن أخي إبراهيم، أرسل إلى أهل سدوم لينهاهم عن الفواحش ويدعوهم إلى الله.

bio.en: Sent to Madyan; commanded worship of Allah alone and fair measure in trade, forbidding corruption.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى مدين، فأمرهم بعبادة الله وإيفاء الكيل والميزان ونهاهم عن الفساد.

bio.en: Son of Yaqub; thrown into a well, sold into Egypt, then raised by Allah through patience and trust to authority.
bio.ar: ابن يعقوب؛ أُلقي في الجبّ ثم بيع بمصر، فرفعه الله بالصبر والتوكل إلى الملك.

bio.en: Patient prophet stricken with severe trial in health and wealth; he turned to Allah and was restored.
bio.ar: نبيٌّ صابر ابتُلي في بدنه وماله، فأناب إلى الله فردّ عليه عافيته.

bio.en: Mentioned among the patient and righteous; Ibn Kathir places him among the prophets of firm resolve in obedience.
bio.ar: ذُكر مع الصابرين والصالحين، وعدّه ابن كثير فيمن ثبتوا على طاعة الله.

bio.en: Left his people in anger, was swallowed by the whale, then called upon Allah in the darkness and was rescued.
bio.ar: غادر قومه مغاضباً فالتقمه الحوت، فنادى الله في الظلمات فنجّاه.

bio.en: Sent to Pharaoh with clear signs; led the Children of Israel and received the Torah.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى فرعون بالآيات، وأخرج بني إسرائيل وأنزلت عليه التوراة.

bio.en: Brother of Musa and a prophet who supported him in calling Pharaoh and guiding the Israelites.
bio.ar: أخو موسى ونبيّ أيّده في دعوة فرعون وهداية بني إسرائيل.

bio.en: Known as Ezekiel; Ibn Kathir recounts him among the prophets after Musa who revived hope for the Israelites.
bio.ar: يُعرف بحزقيال؛ ذكره ابن كثير فيمن بعث بعد موسى لإحياء رجاء بني إسرائيل.

bio.en: Called his people away from idolatry; Ibn Kathir includes him among the prophets between Musa and the later messengers.
bio.ar: دعا قومه لترك الشرك، وعدّه ابن كثير في الأنبياء بين موسى ومن بعدهم.

bio.en: Samuel; appointed when the Israelites asked for a king after defeat, and guided them under Allah’s command.
bio.ar: شمويل؛ بُعث حين طلب بنو إسرائيل ملكاً بعد الهزيمة، فهداهم بأمر الله.

bio.en: Defeated Goliath, was given kingship and the Zabur, and judged with justice and beautiful remembrance of Allah.
bio.ar: هزم جالوت، وآتاه الله الملك والزبور، وقضى بالعدل وأكثر من ذكر الله.

bio.en: Inherited Dawud’s prophethood; taught the speech of birds and given dominion over jinn, men, and the wind.
bio.ar: ورث نبوة داود، وعُلّم منطق الطير وسُخّر له الجنّ والإنس والريح.

bio.en: Isaiah; advised the righteous king of his time and, according to Ibn Kathir, foretold later messengers.
bio.ar: شعيا؛ نصح ملك زمانه الصالح، وذكر ابن كثير أنه بشّر بمن يأتي من الرسل.

bio.en: Jeremiah; warned his people and lived through the trials of Jerusalem as related by Ibn Kathir.
bio.ar: أرميا؛ أنذر قومه وعاش محنة بيت المقدس كما روى ابن كثير.

bio.en: Preserved by Allah when cast among lions; a righteous figure of the Babylonian captivity in Ibn Kathir’s accounts.
bio.ar: نجّاه الله إذ أُلقي إلى الأسود؛ من صلحاء سبي بابل في روايات ابن كثير.

bio.en: Ezra; the Quranic account of one who passed by ruined dwellings and whom Allah caused to die a hundred years then raised.
bio.ar: عزير؛ صاحب قصة من مرّ على قرية خاوية فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه.

bio.en: Elderly prophet who cared for Maryam and prayed for an heir; granted Yahya in his old age.
bio.ar: نبي طاعن في السن كفل مريم ودعا بالذرية، فوُهب يحيى على الكبر.

bio.en: Son of Zakariyah; given wisdom as a child, devout and merciful, holding fast to the Scripture.
bio.ar: ابن زكريا؛ أوتي الحكم صبيّاً، وكان تقيّاً رحيماً آخذاً بالكتاب بقوة.

bio.en: Son of Maryam, created by Allah’s word; a messenger supported with clear signs, not a son of God.
bio.ar: ابن مريم خلقه الله بكلمة منه، رسول مؤيّد بالآيات، وليس ابناً لله.

honorific.en: peace and blessings of Allah be upon him

bio.en: The Messenger of Allah, seal of the prophets.
bio.ar: رسول الله وخاتم النبيين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The first caliph and the closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ.
bio.ar: أول الخلفاء الراشدين وأقرب أصحاب النبي ﷺ.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The second caliph, known as Al-Faruq.
bio.ar: ثاني الخلفاء الراشدين، الملقّب بالفاروق.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The third caliph, known as Dhun-Nurayn.
bio.ar: ثالث الخلفاء الراشدين، الملقّب بذي النورين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The fourth caliph, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ.
bio.ar: رابع الخلفاء الراشدين، ابن عم النبي ﷺ وصهره.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; known as Talhah the Generous.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، يُعرف بطلحة الفيّاض.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; hawari of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، حواري رسول الله ﷺ.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; a trusted merchant and early emigrant.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، تاجر أمين من السابقين المهاجرين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; the first to shoot an arrow in the path of Allah.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، أول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; an early convert from the Quraysh.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، من السابقين إلى الإسلام من قريش.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; Amin of this Ummah.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، أمين هذه الأمة.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with her

bio.en: First wife of the Prophet ﷺ and the first to believe in his message.
bio.ar: زوج النبي ﷺ الأولى وأول من آمن برسالته.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with her

bio.en: Mother of the Believers and a foremost narrator of the Sunnah.
bio.ar: أم المؤمنين ومن أعلم رواة السنة.

honorific.en: may Allah have mercy on him

bio.en: A Tabi'i from Yemen, praised by the Prophet ﷺ for his devotion to his mother.
bio.ar: تابعي من اليمن، أثنى عليه النبي ﷺ لبرّه بوالدته.

content.en: When Ibrahim called his people to tawhid and broke their idols, they kindled a great fire and cast him into it. Allah commanded: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." The fire did not harm him. Ibrahim grew up among people who worshipped idols, stars, and kings. He reasoned that created things cannot be gods and called his father and people to the One Creator. He broke the idols, leaving the largest to expose their falsehood. They cast him into a great fire, but Allah commanded the fire to be coolness and safety upon him. He continued calling to tawhid. Later he left Hajar and Isma‘il in Makkah by Allah’s command, and with Isma‘il raised the foundations of the House. His life is the story of a friend of Allah who preferred truth over his people’s customs. Ibn Kathir gathers these trials to show courage, intellect, and trust in Allah.
content.ar: لما دعا إبراهيم قومه إلى التوحيد وكسّر أصنامهم أوقدوا ناراً عظيمة وألقوه فيها. فقال الله: يا نار كوني برداً وسلاماً على إبراهيم. فلم تمسّه بسوء. نشأ إبراهيم بين من يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب والملوك. فحاجّهم أن المخلوق لا يكون إلهاً، ودعا أباه وقومه إلى الخالق الواحد. وكسّر الأصنام تاركاً كبيرها ليفضح باطلهم. فألقوه في نار عظيمة فجعلها الله برداً وسلاماً عليه. وواصل الدعوة، ثم أسكن هاجر وإسماعيل بمكة بأمر الله، ورفع مع إسماعيل قواعد البيت. فكانت حياته سيرة خليل آثر الحق على عادة قومه. وجمع ابن كثير هذه الابتلاءات لتظهر الشجاعة والعقل والتوكل.

stories.sourceCitation: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets (Qisas al-Anbiya); teaching paraphrase from the English edition

content.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would seclude himself in the cave of Hira. Jibril came to him and said, "Read." He replied, "I am not one who reads." The angel pressed him, then said: "Read in the name of your Lord who created." Thus the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq were revealed.
content.ar: كان رسول الله ﷺ يتحنّث في غار حراء. فجاءه جبريل فقال: اقرأ. قال: ما أنا بقارئ. فغطّه ثم قال: «اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ». فنزلت أوائل سورة العلق.

stories.sourceCitation: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Bad' al-Wahy, Hadith 3

content.en: During the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in the cave of Thawr. Abu Bakr said, "If one of them looks at his feet he will see us." The Prophet ﷺ replied, "What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah?"
content.ar: في الهجرة اختبأ النبي ﷺ وأبو بكر في غار ثور. فقال أبو بكر: لو أن أحدهم نظر إلى قدميه لأبصرنا. فقال النبي ﷺ: «ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما؟»

stories.sourceCitation: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah, Hadith 3653; Quran 9:40

content.en: The Prophet ﷺ told Umar and Ali of a man from Yemen named Uways. He would have a white mark from illness, and he was deeply devoted to his mother. The Prophet ﷺ instructed them: if they met him, to ask him to seek forgiveness for them.
content.ar: أخبر النبي ﷺ عمر وعلياً برجل من اليمن اسمه أويس، به بياض من مرض، وكان بارّاً بوالدته. وأمرهما إن لقياه أن يستغفرا به.

content.en: Musa was saved as a baby from Pharaoh’s killing of sons, raised in the palace, then fled after an accidental killing. At the burning bush Allah spoke to him and sent him with Harun to Pharaoh. They showed clear signs; Pharaoh grew arrogant. Musa led the Children of Israel by night. Trapped between the army and the sea, he said, “Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.” The sea parted, and Pharaoh drowned. Allah revealed the Torah and continued guiding Musa through later trials of his people. Ibn Kathir’s long chapter is a school of courage, reliance, and truth before tyrants.
content.ar: نُجّي موسى رضيعاً من قتل فرعون للذكور، ورُبّي في القصر، ثم خرج بعد قتل خطأ. وعند النار كلّمه الله وأرسله مع هارون إلى فرعون. فأريا الآيات فتكبّر فرعون. وسار موسى ببني إسرائيل ليلاً. فلما حُصر بين الجند والبحر قال إن معي ربي سيهدين، فانفلق البحر وأُغرق فرعون. وأنزلت التوراة، وتتابعت هداية موسى في فتن قومه. وكتاب ابن كثير في موسى مدرسة شجاعة وتوكل وصدق أمام الطغاة.

content.en: Yunus left his people in anger when they delayed belief. A storm rose at sea and he was cast overboard, then swallowed by a great fish. In layers of darkness he called: there is no deity except You; exalted are You; I have been of the wrongdoers. Allah answered him and delivered him. He was cast onto the shore, and Allah caused a plant to grow over him. His people later believed. Ibn Kathir highlights the famous prayer of relief.
content.ar: غادر يونس قومه مغاضباً لتأخر إيمانهم. فهاج البحر وأُلقي ثم التقمه الحوت. فنادى في الظلمات: لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين. فاستجاب الله ونجّاه. وأُلقي إلى الشاطئ وأنبت الله عليه شجرة، وآمن قومه من بعد. ويبرز ابن كثير دعاء الفرج المشهور.

timedCues.textAr: وأُلقي إلى الشاطئ وأنبت الله عليه شجرة، وآمن قومه من بعد. ويبرز ابن كثير دعاء الفرج المشهور.

content.en: Allah told the angels He would place successive generations on earth. He taught Adam the names of all things, then asked the angels to name them. They admitted they knew only what Allah had taught them, and Adam spoke by Allah’s teaching, showing the honor given to humankind. Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam as a mark of respect. Iblis refused out of arrogance and was expelled. Adam was placed in Paradise with his wife. They were forbidden one tree; after they slipped, they repented, and Allah accepted their repentance. They were sent to earth to live, worship, and raise children upon tawhid. Adam called his offspring to Allah until his death, longing for Paradise and leaving a covenant of guidance for those after him. Ibn Kathir gathers these reports from the Quran and early narrations so that Adam’s story teaches dignity, repentance, and the danger of pride.
content.ar: أخبر الله الملائكة أنه جاعل في الأرض خلفاء، وعلّم آدم الأسماء كلها، ثم سأل الملائكة أن ينبئوه بها. فقالوا لا علم لنا إلا ما علّمتنا، فأنبأهم آدم بما علّمه الله، إظهاراً لتكريم الإنسان. وأمر الله الملائكة بالسجود لآدم تحيةً، فأبى إبليس استكباراً فأُخرج. وأسكن آدم وزوجته الجنة، ونُهيا عن شجرة، فلما زلّا تابا فتاب الله عليهما. ثم أُهبطا إلى الأرض ليعبدوا الله ويربّوا الذرية على التوحيد. فظل آدم يدعو بنيه حتى وفاته، تائقاً إلى الجنة تاركاً عهد الهداية. وجمع ابن كثير ذلك من القرآن والآثار ليعلّم الكرامة والتوبة وخطر الكبر.

He and his followers moved on, continuing to teach what is fair. The Quran praises him as truthful and a prophet whom Allah raised to a high station. Ibn Kathir presents Idris among the earliest guides after Adam, a reminder that prophethood continued whenever people drifted from Allah’s way.

title.en: The Story of Nuh and the Ark

content.en: Nuh called his people for a very long time to leave idols and worship Allah alone. The chiefs mocked him and said he was in error, yet he answered with patience that he was only a messenger bringing sincere advice. By Allah’s command he built the Ark. When the Flood began, believers boarded with pairs of creatures. Nuh’s son sought a mountain instead of Allah’s mercy and was among the drowned. Then the earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to withhold rain. The Ark rested, and the wrongdoers were destroyed. The story remains a sign for those who take heed. Ibn Kathir walks through these scenes from the Quran so that believers learn steadfastness in calling to tawhid.
content.ar: دعا نوح قومه زمناً طويلاً إلى ترك الأصنام وعبادة الله وحده. فسخر منه الملأ وقالوا إنه في ضلال، فصبر وقال إنما هو رسول ناصح. وصنع السفينة بأمر الله. فلما جاء الطوفان ركب المؤمنون ومعهم من كل زوجين اثنين. وطلب ابنه جبلاً يعصمه فكان من المغرقين. ثم قيل للأرض أن تبلع ماءها وللسماء أن تقلع، واستوت السفينة وهلك الظالمون. وبقيت القصة آية لمن يعتبر. ويسوق ابن كثير ذلك من القرآن ليعلّم الثبات على دعوة التوحيد.

content.en: The people of ‘Ad lived between Yemen and Oman. They were strong builders of tall structures, wealthy and proud. They knew of Allah yet joined idols with Him. Hud, one of them, called them to worship Allah alone and warned of a Day when deeds are judged. They listened but disbelieved, and asked for the punishment to be hastened. What they thought was a rain-cloud was a destructive wind by Allah’s command. It ruined everything they trusted in. Hud and those who believed were saved. Ibn Kathir frames ‘Ad as a warning against arrogance born of power and wealth.
content.ar: سكنت عاد بين اليمن وعُمان، أشدّاء بنّائين للأبراج، أغنياء متكبرين. عرفوا الله ثم أشركوا معه الأصنام. فدعاهم هود من أنفسهم إلى التوحيد وحذّرهم يوم الحساب. فسمعوا وكذّبوا واستعجلوا العذاب. فكان السحاب الذي رجوا مطره ريحاً مدمّرة بأمر الله أهلكت ما كانوا فيه يثقون. ونجّى الله هوداً ومن آمن. ويعرض ابن كثير عاد عبرةً من الكبر عند القوة والغنى.

title.en: The Story of Salih and the She-Camel

content.en: After ‘Ad, Thamud rose in power. They carved beautiful homes in the hills yet fell into idolatry and oppression. Salih called them to worship Allah alone. As a clear sign, Allah brought forth the she-camel. Some believed, but many complained and plotted to kill the camel and harm Salih. Allah saved Salih and the believers. After his warning, a crushing cry destroyed the wrongdoers. The valley that once boasted of its craftsmanship became a lesson. Ibn Kathir stresses that rejecting clear signs after they arrive brings ruin.
content.ar: بعد عاد ارتفعت ثمود، فنحتوا بيوتاً في الجبال ووقعوا في الشرك والظلم. فدعاهم صالح إلى عبادة الله وحده. وجعل الله الناقة آية بينة. فآمن بعضٌ وتآمر آخرون على عقرها وأذى صالح. فنجّى الله صالحاً والمؤمنين، وأهلك الظالمين بالصيحة بعد إنذاره. وصار الوادي الذي افتخر ببنائه عبرة. ويؤكّد ابن كثير أن ردّ الآيات بعد مجيئها سبب للهلاك.

content.en: Ibrahim grew up among people who worshipped idols, stars, and kings. He reasoned that created things cannot be gods and called his father and people to the One Creator. He broke the idols, leaving the largest to expose their falsehood. They cast him into a great fire, but Allah commanded the fire to be coolness and safety upon him. He continued calling to tawhid. Later he left Hajar and Isma‘il in Makkah by Allah’s command, and with Isma‘il raised the foundations of the House. His life is the story of a friend of Allah who preferred truth over his people’s customs. Ibn Kathir gathers these trials to show courage, intellect, and trust in Allah.
content.ar: نشأ إبراهيم بين من يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب والملوك. فحاجّهم أن المخلوق لا يكون إلهاً، ودعا أباه وقومه إلى الخالق الواحد. وكسّر الأصنام تاركاً كبيرها ليفضح باطلهم. فألقوه في نار عظيمة فجعلها الله برداً وسلاماً عليه. وواصل الدعوة، ثم أسكن هاجر وإسماعيل بمكة بأمر الله، ورفع مع إسماعيل قواعد البيت. فكانت حياته سيرة خليل آثر الحق على عادة قومه. وجمع ابن كثير هذه الابتلاءات لتظهر الشجاعة والعقل والتوكل.

title.en: The Story of Isma‘il and Zamzam

content.en: Ibrahim brought Hajar and their nursing son Isma‘il to a barren valley with little water, then left them by Allah’s command. When the water finished, Hajar ran between the hills seeking help until Zamzam sprang forth. Ibrahim returned at times Allah willed. With Isma‘il he raised the foundations of the Ka‘bah. Isma‘il remained patient in that sanctuary, a prophet in the line of Ibrahim. Ibn Kathir links this valley to mercy: water, house, and a people who would later receive the final messenger.
content.ar: جاء إبراهيم بهاجر وابنها إسماعيل الرضيع إلى وادٍ غير ذي زرع بقليل من الماء، وتركهما بأمر الله. فلما نفد الماء سعت هاجر بين الصفا والمروة حتى نبع زمزم. وعاد إبراهيم حين شاء الله، فرفع مع إسماعيل قواعد الكعبة. وبقي إسماعيل صابراً في الحرم نبياً من آل إبراهيم. ويربط ابن كثير هذا الوادي بالرحمة: ماءٌ وبيتٌ وأمة سيأتيها الخاتم.

content.en: Glad tidings of Ishaq came to Ibrahim in old age. Commentators related that Ibrahim sought for him a righteous wife from his kin, not from pagan Canaanites. From Ishaq came Yaqub, continuing the prophetic line. Though the Quran gives few details of Ishaq’s personal life, he is named among the guided prophets. Ibn Kathir places him as a link of blessing between Ibrahim and the Children of Israel.
content.ar: بُشّر إبراهيم بإسحاق على الكبر. وذكر المفسرون أنه طلب له زوجة صالحة من أهله لا من الكنعانيين المشركين. ومن إسحاق جاء يعقوب فامتدت سلسلة النبوة. وقلّ تفصيل حياته في القرآن، وهو معدود في الأنبياء المهتدين. ويجعله ابن كثير حلقة بركة بين إبراهيم وبني إسرائيل.

content.en: Yaqub, also called Israel, was favored with prophethood. Tension with his brother led him to travel and seek Allah’s protection with prayer and humility. He fathered the twelve tribes and loved Yusuf deeply. When Yusuf was taken, Yaqub’s eyes whitened with grief, yet he never despaired of Allah’s mercy. His reunion with Yusuf taught patience and beautiful reliance. Ibn Kathir recounts this as a father’s faith under long sorrow.
content.ar: يُدعى يعقوب إسرائيل، وآتاه الله النبوة. ووقع بينه وبين أخيه ما حمله على الرحيل والاستعاذة بالله خاشعاً. ورزق الأسباط، وكان أشد حباً ليوسف. فلما فُقد يوسف ابيضّت عيناه من الحزن ولم ييأس من رحمة الله. وكان اجتماعه بيوسف درس صبر وحسن ظن. ويذكره ابن كثير إيمان أبٍ في حزن طويل.

timedCues.textEn: He fathered the twelve tribes and loved Yusuf deeply. When Yusuf was taken, Yaqub’s eyes whitened with grief, yet he never despaired of Allah’s mercy.
timedCues.textAr: ورزق الأسباط، وكان أشد حباً ليوسف. فلما فُقد يوسف ابيضّت عيناه من الحزن ولم ييأس من رحمة الله.

timedCues.textEn: His reunion with Yusuf taught patience and beautiful reliance. Ibn Kathir recounts this as a father’s faith under long sorrow.
timedCues.textAr: وكان اجتماعه بيوسف درس صبر وحسن ظن. ويذكره ابن كثير إيمان أبٍ في حزن طويل.

content.en: Lut settled near Sodom, a city known for highway robbery and open indecency. He called them to fear Allah and leave their wrongdoing, but they threatened him instead. Angels came as guests. The people rushed toward them. Lut was taken out by night with his believing household, and the town was overturned as a warning. Ibn Kathir presents the account as a severe lesson: mocking purity and harming guests invites destruction.
content.ar: سكن لوط قرب سدوم حيث قطع الطريق والفواحش المجاهرة. فدعاهم إلى تقوى الله وترك المنكر فهددوه. وجاءته الملائكة أضيافاً فهجم القوم. فأُخرج لوط ليلاً ومن آمن من أهله، وقُلبت القرية عبرة. ويعرض ابن كثير القصة درساً شديداً: أن السخرية من الطهر وإيذاء الضيف سبب للهلاك.

content.en: Shu‘aib was sent to Madyan: worship Allah alone, give full measure and weight, and do not corrupt the land or block the path of believers. They ridiculed him and clung to cheating in trade. After clear warning, a cry and torment seized the wrongdoers while believers were saved. Ibn Kathir ties this story to honesty in the marketplace as part of faith.
content.ar: أرسل شعيب إلى مدين: اعبدوا الله وأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تفسدوا في الأرض ولا تصدّوا عن سبيل الله. فاستهزؤوا وتمسكوا بالغش في التجارة. فأخذت الظالمين الصيحة والعذاب ونجّى الله المؤمنين. ويربط ابن كثير القصة بأمانة السوق من شعب الإيمان.

content.en: Yusuf’s brothers, jealous of their father’s love, cast him into a well. Travelers drew him out and sold him in Egypt. There he grew in beauty and character, resisted temptation, and chose prison over sin. In prison he interpreted dreams by Allah’s leave. When the king’s dream was explained, Yusuf was raised to authority over the storehouses. He met his brothers again without revenge, then reunited with Yaqub. The Quran calls this the best of stories. Ibn Kathir unfolds its turns so that patience, chastity, and forgiveness shine after hardship.

content.en: Ayyub was granted health, family, and wealth. Then he was severely tested in body and property. He remained grateful and turned to Allah with a humble plea. Allah answered him, removed his affliction, and restored his family as a mercy. The patient are remembered with honor. Ibn Kathir keeps Ayyub as the model of steadfast praise in long trial.
content.ar: أوتي أيوب الصحة والأهل والمال، ثم ابتُلي في بدنه وماله بلاء شديداً. فبقي شاكراً وأناب إلى الله بدعاء خاشع. فاستجاب الله وكشف ضرّه وردّ أهله رحمة. ويُذكر الصابرون بثناء. ويبقى أيوب عند ابن كثير إمام الحمد في طول البلاء.

content.en: Dhul-Kifl is mentioned with the patient and righteous. Ibn Kathir places him among those steadfast in obedience and judgment. Though details are fewer than for other prophets, his mention teaches constancy upon the trust Allah places on His servants. The lesson is not length of narration but firmness upon what Allah commands.

content.en: When Musa feared he would not speak clearly, Allah appointed his brother Harun as prophet and helper. Together they went to Pharaoh with clear proofs. Harun stood with Musa in calling to Allah and guiding the Children of Israel. In later trials he sought to keep the people from splitting until Musa returned. Ibn Kathir shows Harun as sincere support in conveying the message—eloquence joined to brotherhood.
content.ar: لما خشي موسى ألا يفصح لسانه جعل الله أخاه هارون نبياً ووزيراً. فذهبا معاً إلى فرعون بالبينات. وثبت هارون مع موسى في الدعوة وهداية بني إسرائيل. وفي الفتن حرص على ألا يتفرّقوا حتى يرجع موسى. ويظهره ابن كثير نصرة صادقة للرسالة: فصاحة مع أخوّة.

content.en: Ibn Kathir recounts Hizqeel (Ezekiel) among prophets after Musa when the Israelites needed renewal of hope and obedience. Reports describe guidance that revived hearts after fear and loss. Whether every detail is equally strong, the core lesson stands: Allah sends reminders whenever communities grow weak. The account keeps hope alive after great messengers have passed.
content.ar: ذكر ابن كثير حزقيل فيمن بعث بعد موسى حين احتاج بنو إسرائيل لتجديد الرجاء والطاعة. وترد أخبار عن هداية أحيت القلوب بعد الخوف والخسارة. ومع تفاوت قوة التفاصيل يبقى الأصل: أن الله يرسل المذكرين كلما ضعف الناس. فتبقى القصة رجاءً بعد ذهاب كبار الرسل.

content.en: Ilyas called his people to leave idolatry and return to Allah alone. Ibn Kathir includes him among prophets between Musa and later messengers. His message matches the shared call of the prophets: worship is for Allah alone, and idols cannot benefit or harm. Steadfast calling in a forgetful age is the heart of his story.
content.ar: دعا إلياس قومه لترك الأصنام والرجوع إلى الله وحده. وعدّه ابن كثير بين موسى ومن بعده. ورسالته رسالة الأنبياء: العبادة لله وحده، والأصنام لا تنفع ولا تضر. والثبات على الدعوة في زمن الغفلة لبّ قصته.

content.en: After defeat and the loss of the Ark, the Israelites asked for a prophet to appoint a king. Allah sent Shammil (Samuel). He guided them under revelation, warned about the burdens of kingship, and tested who would obey Allah’s limits before battle. Ibn Kathir uses this episode to show that victory follows obedience more than numbers.

content.en: When Goliath challenged Saul’s army, young Dawud stepped forward while others feared. Allah gave him victory over the giant. Dawud was later given kingship and the Zabur. He judged with justice and was known for beautiful remembrance of Allah. Trials refined him when he hastened in judgment and then sought forgiveness. Ibn Kathir balances courage, worship, and humility in a prophet-king.

content.en: Sulaiman inherited prophethood—not wealth—from Dawud. Allah taught him the speech of birds and subjected jinn, men, and the wind to his command. When the Queen of Sheba sent gifts, he refused alliance by wealth and called her to submit to Allah. His hosts of men, jinn, and birds marched in order by Allah’s leave. Ibn Kathir joins power with gratitude: dominion is a trust, not a toy.

content.en: Shi‘a (Isaiah) lived between Dawud’s line and Zakariyah. Ibn Kathir relates that he advised an obedient king and warned of invading armies. He called rulers and people back to Allah and spoke of messengers yet to come. Counsel to the powerful is itself a form of prophethood’s burden. The story urges leaders to listen before pride destroys a city.

content.en: Aramaya (Jeremiah) warned his people as injustice grew. Ibn Kathir describes siege and harsh rule that followed disobedience. content.en: Elderly Zakariyah cared for Maryam in the sanctuary and saw out-of-season provision with her. He prayed for a pure heir despite old age and barrenness. Allah gave him glad tidings of Yahya and a sign that he would not speak to people for three nights though unimpaired. He came out signaling them to glorify Allah. Ibn Kathir paints tenderness: an old prophet’s prayer answered against every ordinary limit.

content.en: Yahya was serious and merciful from childhood, given wisdom while still young and commanded to hold fast to the Scripture. He lived simply, warning people and judging by Allah’s guidance, devoted to purity and remembrance. Beasts felt safe around him as he praised Allah in the open. Ibn Kathir remembers a youth whose strength was piety, not play.

content.en: Isa son of Maryam was created by Allah’s word without a father, a messenger supported with clear signs. The Quran rejects claims that Allah has a son or that He is one of three. He called to worship Allah alone, affirmed earlier scripture, and stood against empty materialism. His miraculous birth and mission are signs of Allah’s power and mercy—not a share in divinity. Ibn Kathir closes the prophetic line before Muhammad ﷺ by affirming Isa’s honor as Abdullah, the servant and messenger of Allah.
content.ar: خلق الله عيسى ابن مريم بكلمة منه من غير أب، رسولاً مؤيداً بالبينات. ونفى القرآن أن يكون لله ولد أو أنه ثالث ثلاثة. فدعا إلى عبادة الله وحده وصدّق ما بين يديه، ووقف ضد مادية جوفاء. فميلاده ومعجزاته آية لقدرة الله ورحمته لا شرك في الألوهية. ويختم ابن كثير ما قبل محمد ﷺ بتقرير أن عيسى عبد الله ورسوله.
